To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transient photoconductivity response of a semiconductor MQW system in the nanoseconde regime exhibits saturation and that this behaviour can be attributed to the density dependence of electron mobility in the electron-hole plasma.

the transient photoconductivity in semiconductor MQW systems exhibits a sublinear intensity dependence and that the origin of such behaviour can be understood as a consequence of the density dependence on mobility of the electron-hole plasma.
we have measured the density dependence of electron mobility in a semiconductor MQW system and that this dependence is consistent with the presence of the electron-hole plasma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the transient response of the photocurrent in a semiconductor MQW structure.
the development and application of photoconductivity techniques for the measurement of the carrier mobility in semiconductor quantum well structures.
the investigation of photoconductivity of MQW systems in order to study the electron mobility in these structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electron mobility in a plasma is reduced by a factor of 2-4 in comparison with the mobility of the free electrons in the absence of plasma.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electron mobility in a quantum well system is reduced from its value in bulk material due to the presence of the quantum subband structure.
we have shown that the transient photoconduction response of semiconductor MQWs can be used as a sensitive probe for the density dependence of electron mobility.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the photoconductive response in a quantum well system is not a simple function of the plasma density, but is also strongly influenced by the density-dependent electron mobility.
the mobility of an electron-hole plasma can be significantly different from the mobility in the absence of a hole plasma.
the electron mobility in a degenerate electron-hole plasma is significantly reduced by the subband structure, and this reduction is more pronounced for lower electron densities.
